source: Revenue Management Labs, "Pricing and Packaging Recommendations — Enablement Discussion," Sept 2026, plus the Sept 16 GTM pricing/packaging working session.
summary: Today, Grace Hill's point solutions (Training, Surveys, Policies, Mystery Shopping, Reputation Management, Intelligence+, Realync, HelloData®) are each priced and packaged on their own, with no shared PHQ commercial structure. Result: no ready-to-go package puts related solutions together, ~79% of GH-Success and ~50% of Mid-Market/Enterprise customers buy only one product, and there's no clear expansion path. The new structure organizes around the two workflows buyers actually own — Workforce Excellence (L&D/Ops) and Resident & Prospect Satisfaction (Marketing) — with data & intelligence as a connective layer across both, and a standardized per-unit commercial model. It is a three-decision purchase: (1) pick your workflow track(s), (2) pick your data & intelligence tier, (3) add add-ons as needed.

buyerGroups.question: How do we onboard and develop employees, manage compliance and policy requirements, and assess/improve on-site performance?
How do we understand resident and prospect sentiment, strengthen reputation and attract prospects, and improve leasing engagement and conversion?
How do we benchmark market performance and competitive position?

packagingGuidelines.why: No single buyer owns the full Grace Hill portfolio; needs and budgets sit across distinct functional teams.
packagingGuidelines.response: Organize around the workflows buyers already own — Workforce Excellence for L&D/Ops, Resident & Prospect Satisfaction for Marketing.

packagingGuidelines.why: Customers, especially larger operators, want to start with a focused need and expand as value is proven.
packagingGuidelines.response: Preserve clear entry points with a path to broader adoption: Core → Plus → cross-track.

packagingGuidelines.guideline: Data & Intelligence as the connective layer
packagingGuidelines.why: Connected data, cross-product insights and AI are increasingly important sources of platform value.
packagingGuidelines.response: Connect workflows through a shared PHQ intelligence layer — Core across every package, Plus for deeper intelligence and integration.

packagingGuidelines.why: Competitors are unifying point solutions into a clear package progression with a standardized pricing unit.
packagingGuidelines.response: Standardize the core commercial logic: common per-unit pricing, consistent tiers, targeted add-ons.

architecture.step: 1 of 3 — choose your workflow track(s). Everything priced per unit per month unless noted; additional mystery shops priced per shop.

tracks.outcomeFraming: People performance: develop people and drive operational consistency.

includes: 4 core policy modules: Emergency, Management & Operations, Maintenance, Leasing & Marketing
Extended training access (role-specific courses + full Spark access)
Semi-annual mystery shops per property/year + upskill training
Quarterly mystery shops per property/year + upskill training

tracks.outcomeFraming: Property performance: improve the resident and prospect experience.

includes: Resident and prospect surveys (SKU: MTM Multifamily Essentials) + Kingsley Index benchmarking
Realync Core: hosting + general sharing + integrations + analytics + video recording/editing + tracked sharing + live video tour
Includes both cores — Sentiment and Leasing
Extended survey benchmarks by class & market (roadmap feature, not yet shipped)

tracks.note: Sentiment Core and Leasing Core are two distinct entry points for two distinct needs — they don't build on each other. A customer who only wants Realync buys Leasing Core, not a step on the way to Sentiment Core. Plus is the option that bundles both.

dataIntelligenceLayer.step: 2 of 3 — choose your data & intelligence tier. Included with every track purchase; not sold standalone to PHQ buyers.

includes: HelloData® Taster (limited locations + limited comps + limited KPIs)
Data integration through exposed APIs and an MCP connector for AI assistants

dataIntelligenceLayer.note: A $0.20/unit Platform Core price is embedded in every track's list price; it is netted out for customers buying across tracks to avoid double-counting. HelloData® also continues to exist as its own standalone purchase for 'HelloData® purists' (e.g., banks, investment institutions doing acquisition diligence) who explicitly do not want the PHQ platform — that entry point is not going away.

addOns.step: 3 of 3 — add-ons, sold outside the tier structure.
addOns.note: Existing implementation fees and niche-use-case add-ons (custom implementation, FTP feed, commercial/construction/tax-credit courses and manuals, CRE manual, employee results presentations, survey customization, custom resident data integration, survey translation) remain priced and structured as-is — no changes recommended. Realync add-on pricing (Real360, Realync Journeys, Realync Studios) has moved to a per-unit basis.
addOns.mysteryShopFlexibility: Default included shop is Onsite (Non-Recorded) + Phone (Recorded/Non-Recorded), at semi-annual frequency in Core and quarterly in Plus. Customers can swap shop type (e.g., add Internet, upgrade to Audio or Video recording) at their included frequency without changing tier. Increasing frequency beyond what's included (e.g., twice-a-quarter, monthly) requires being on Plus — frequency upgrades don't create a back-door path around the Core→Plus decision. Customers can also always buy additional on-demand/a-la-carte shops above what's in the package.

discountFramework.how: Discount for adopting additional tracks; rewards power users.
discountFramework.recommended: Cross-track buyer (both tracks): 8%. Power user (all Plus): 10%. Replaces today's 0% / 5% / 8% by count-of-solutions ladder — every new package already has a bundled discount baked into its list price, so the old “buy a 2nd point solution, get 5% off” step goes away.

discountFramework.how: Standardized unit-count tiers; per-unit rate falls as the portfolio grows.
discountFramework.recommended: Same step-downs across every package: 1,000–3,999 = list; 4,000–9,999 = -10%; 10,000–19,999 = -17.5%; 20,000+ = -17.5%. Today the buckets and rates vary by point solution (lowest: Training, highest: Policies) — this standardizes them.

Proposed in the deck as a new 10% discount for 3+ year terms, standard annual price increases still apply. CONTESTED IN THE ROOM (Sept 16): Sales leadership (Ashlee Horn) pushed back hard on making a multi-year discount standard — 56% of this quarter's contracts sold multi-year with no discount offered, and giving away margin by default risks eating into deal size given packages are already bundled/discounted. RML (Navi) agreed to take it offline and revisit an alternative: 3-year term as the standard list price, with a modest premium for a more flexible 1- or 2-year term, rather than a discount for going long. Do not present the 10%-for-3-years figure as settled until this is resolved.

discountFramework.how: Applied case-by-case at the deal level.
discountFramework.recommended: No change recommended. New sales: up to 5% auto-approved, >5-10% Sales Director, >10-18% VP, >18% CRO. Renewals: 8%+ resulting price increase auto-approved, 5-<8% CS Director, <5% VP+.

buyerMatchFramework.problemFirstNote: Ashlee Horn flagged in the Sept 16 working session that this buyer-first / persona-first framing reads as a step back from the problem-based selling motion the team has spent Q1–Q2 training reps on, and that it doesn't sound like how the sales team talks to customers today. Mandy agreed and proposed reframing: instead of opening with “who's the buyer,” open with the outcome the buyer cares about — people performance outcomes (Track 1) versus property performance outcomes (Track 2) — and let the buyer-match questions above sit underneath that framing as the configuration logic, not the opening pitch. This buyer-match table is the internal package-selection tool for reps; the customer-facing conversation should lead with the problemFirstMessaging block below, not with these six questions.

problemFirstMessaging.howToUse: Outside-in, VBF order (Value → Benefit → Feature) per Grace Hill's messaging framework: open with the problem/outcome the buyer already cares about, then the benefit, then how Grace Hill delivers it — the package and its features come last, as the mechanism, not the headline. This directly answers the reframe Mandy and Ashlee agreed to on the Sept 16 call: stop opening with ‘who is the buyer’ and start with the outcome.

tracks.problem: Your team's execution is inconsistent from property to property, compliance risk sits on whoever happens to be on shift, and you can't tell whether that's a training gap, a policy gap, or a people problem until something has already gone wrong.
tracks.outcome: People performance: every employee, at every property, working to the same standard — fewer compliance incidents, faster onboarding, and execution that doesn't depend on your one strong regional manager.
tracks.benefit: You get ahead of the audit or the incident instead of reacting to it, and you can prove — not just hope — that your team is trained, policy-acknowledged, and performing to standard.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Training, policies, and mystery shopping working together under one PHQ Platform — industry-specific courseware, policy acknowledgment tracking, and on-site performance verification — packaged as Compliance, Core, or Plus depending on how far past baseline compliance you need to go.

tracks.problem: You don't have a reliable read on how residents and prospects actually feel about your properties until they leave a bad review, don't renew, or don't tour — and by then it's too late to do anything but react.
tracks.outcome: Property performance: leasing and retention that improve because you catch sentiment and friction early — in the resident relationship and in the leasing funnel — instead of finding out from a lost renewal or a 2-star review.
tracks.benefit: Fewer surprises at renewal, a reputation that supports (instead of undercuts) your marketing spend, and a leasing experience that converts more of the tours you're already paying for.
tracks.howWeDeliverIt: Resident and prospect surveys, reputation management, and Realync's leasing video tools working off the same PHQ data layer — packaged as Sentiment Core, Leasing Core, or Plus depending on whether the bigger gap is sentiment, conversion, or both.

sharedLayer.problem: You're making decisions about your portfolio without knowing how you stack up against the market — rents, comps, competitive positioning — which means every pricing and positioning call is a guess.
sharedLayer.outcome: Confidence that your people-performance and property-performance decisions are grounded in real market data, not internal signals alone.
sharedLayer.howWeDeliverIt: HelloData®, included as a taster in every PHQ package and available at full depth in Plus — or standalone for teams (e.g., acquisitions, investment) that only need market data, not the workflow tracks.

purchasingFlexibility.scenario: A third-party operator manages properties for multiple ownership groups with different priorities — e.g., wants Workforce Core broadly across the portfolio, but only certain ownership groups want Realync/Leasing Core.

options.what: Standard packages applied across defined portfolio subsets — different subsets of properties can be on different tracks/tiers, pricing follows the units within each subset, requires eligibility and approval guardrails.
Custom configuration for a complex account; package can vary property by property. Highest quoting and administrative burden; reserved where account complexity/economics justify it.

purchasingFlexibility.guardrail: GH Success and lower Mid-Market remain on a single standard package configuration across the portfolio, without property-level mix-and-match.

objectionHandling.q: Why are you changing the way Grace Hill is packaged? How does this benefit me?
objectionHandling.a: We're simplifying how customers buy Grace Hill. Instead of buying related capabilities one product at a time, you start with the business need and a package built around it — fewer buying decisions and a clearer path to expand over time.

objectionHandling.q: Why should I choose Grace Hill instead of a competitor?
objectionHandling.a: Grace Hill brings together a breadth of multifamily capabilities that's hard to replicate with a single alternative. You solve more needs within one ecosystem, and the value multiplies as those capabilities work together through PHQ rather than across disconnected systems.

objectionHandling.q: Why should I consolidate more of my technology with Grace Hill?
objectionHandling.a: Consolidation simplifies your tech stack and unlocks the additional value of PHQ Intelligence+ — training, policies, performance measurement, resident feedback, leasing and market signals informing one another instead of sitting in separate systems.

objectionHandling.q: I only need Training / Surveys / Realync. Why do I need to move to a broader package?
objectionHandling.a: You don't need to buy the entire Grace Hill ecosystem. Start with the narrowest standard package that solves the need you have today, then expand only when another use case becomes relevant. The packages themselves stay intact — this preserves focused entry points without recreating à-la-carte complexity.

objectionHandling.q: Do all of my properties have to be on the same package?
objectionHandling.a: No. We can match the package to the parts of your portfolio where it makes sense, rather than forcing every property into the same configuration. GH Success and lower Mid-Market stay on one standard configuration; for eligible larger portfolios, Guided Flexibility can apply different standard packages across defined property groups; true property-level customization is Bespoke/CPQ, reserved for strategic accounts.

objectionHandling.q: My unit count changes throughout the year. How do you account for that?
objectionHandling.a: Pricing adjusts with your portfolio — we reconcile unit counts monthly, so additions and removals are reflected as your portfolio changes rather than locking you to the unit count at signing. This is the same process Grace Hill uses today.

objectionHandling.q: What if I need more mystery shops, or want to allocate them differently across my portfolio?
objectionHandling.a: You have flexibility beyond what's included in the package. Core includes semi-annual shops and Plus includes quarterly, but you can change the shop type or increase the frequency based on your needs, and you can always purchase additional shops on demand, above what's in the package.

objectionHandling.q: I only want a one-year contract. Why do I have to commit to multiple years?
objectionHandling.a: You don't have to — one-year contracts remain available. NOTE: the exact multi-year incentive structure (discount-for-3-years vs. premium-for-flexibility) was still being resolved as of Sept 16 — see discountFramework.

objectionHandling.q: This is a big price increase. Why should I pay more?
objectionHandling.a: The new price reflects a broader set of capabilities than what you're buying today, not simply a higher price for the same product. We'll work with you to make sure the package matches the needs you actually have, and if the change is significant, we can help manage the transition over time.
